topics.title: Americans worry AI is moving fast
topics.summary: A new AP-NORC poll found many U.S. adults think artificial intelligence is developing too quickly and want clearer human control as the technology spreads.
topics.discussionPrompt: If AI is sprinting ahead, who wants a big red pause button and who just wants a better instruction manual?

topics.title: Anne Carson wins literature Nobel
topics.summary: Canadian writer Anne Carson won the 2026 Nobel Prize in literature, recognized for genre-crossing work that blends poetry, classics, essays and experimentation.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a writer refuses to stay in one lane, who calls it genius and who asks which shelf the book even goes on?

topics.title: Energy prices jump on shipping worries
topics.summary: Oil and gas prices rose as tanker attacks in the Middle East and hurricane risks near U.S. Gulf output added fresh pressure to markets.
topics.discussionPrompt: When fuel prices jump because of weather and shipping routes, who maps the global chain and who blames their next grocery bill?

topics.title: Myanmar leader courts Malaysia ties
topics.summary: Myanmar's military-backed leader visited Malaysia for talks, part of a diplomatic push after years of regional pressure over the country's political crisis.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a heavily isolated leader starts a charm tour, who watches the handshake photos and who watches what actually changes afterward?

topics.title: NATO spending pressure continues
topics.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said American pressure on NATO allies to spend more on defense is not hostile, while visiting Portugal for talks.
topics.discussionPrompt: When allies argue over who pays for security, who brings out the group dinner analogy and who starts auditing everyone’s receipts?

topics.title: Asos reports customer data hack
topics.summary: Asos said customer names, contact details and search histories were hacked, raising concerns that attackers could use the information for convincing scams.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a store loses your search history, who worries about fraud first and who worries everyone now knows their weird shopping phase?

topics.title: White House press ban reaches court
topics.summary: A federal judge heard arguments over the White House banning CNN, Politico and MS Now from its grounds, keeping press access in the spotlight.
topics.discussionPrompt: When press access becomes a courtroom fight, who quotes free speech principles and who asks how anyone gets a hallway interview now?

topics.title: UK banknotes choose nature theme
topics.summary: The next UK banknotes will feature native species including barn owls, bumblebees, puffins and hedgehogs after a public consultation.
topics.discussionPrompt: If money gets wildlife portraits, who campaigns for the cutest bill and who argues the bee deserves the biggest denomination?

topics.title: Workplace AI monitoring faces scrutiny
topics.summary: Co-op became the latest major employer criticized for putting staff under AI surveillance, adding to debates about privacy, productivity and trust at work.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your boss used AI to watch productivity, who would game the system and who would write a polite complaint in all caps?

topics.title: Students admit procrastination problem
topics.summary: A UK university survey found students see procrastination as a major threat to academic performance, more than some traditional study worries.
topics.discussionPrompt: When procrastination gets named the villain, who says they work better under pressure and who demands the phone go in a drawer?
